subject: Art & Design
title: Le Corbusier's Five Points of Modern Architecture
description: One-minute skill: Le Corbusier's Five Points of Modern Architecture.

hook.text: Pilotis, free plan, free facade, ribbon windows, roof garden. Five rules that reshaped how the world builds.

buildup.text: Le Corbusier published these five principles in 1927, arguing that modern technology demanded a new architecture.

discovery.text: Pilotis (stilts) lift the building, freeing the ground. Free plans let walls go anywhere.

twist.text: His Unité d'Habitation was praised as visionary housing. Many imitations became soulless concrete blocks.

climax.text: His chapel at Ronchamp broke his own rules — proving that even manifestos have limits.

punchline.text: The goal is not certainty, but sharper thinking.

quiz.question: What do 'pilotis' achieve in Le Corbusier's five points?
options: They lift the building on stilts, freeing the ground level
They add decorative columns to the facade

details.summary: Le Corbusier's Five Points — pilotis (columns), free plan, free facade, ribbon windows, and roof garden — defined modern architecture's structural logic. By lifting buildings on columns, structure was freed from walls, allowing open interiors and continuous glazing. Villa Savoye embodies all five.
details.whyItMatters: The Five Points provided a systematic framework for modern architecture. They showed how reinforced concrete could liberate design from load-bearing walls, creating the open-plan living spaces that became universal in 20th-century buildings.
takeaways: Pilotis lift buildings off the ground on columns
Free plan and free facade separate structure from enclosure
Villa Savoye is the purest expression of all five principles

faq.question: What are the Five Points of Modern Architecture?
faq.answer: Pilotis (slender columns raising the building), a free floor plan (no load-bearing interior walls), a free facade (exterior walls independent of structure), horizontal ribbon windows, and a roof garden replacing the ground displaced by the building's footprint.

faq.question: Why is Le Corbusier controversial?
faq.answer: His urban plans proposed demolishing historic neighborhoods for tower blocks in parks. Implemented poorly by followers, this approach produced the sterile housing projects that blighted cities worldwide. His personal authoritarian tendencies and political associations add further controversy.
